title: Steward slice 1, prevent: Monitor-launched sessions can read and are trusted for their own project's worktree root in the default fleet layout (~/.herdr-monitor/p/<hash>/worktrees), so a supervisor reading its lanes' reports never meets Claude's 'read outside the working directories' prompt and Codex workers never meet 'Folder access' for Monitor worktrees; per-launch native settings only, never the operator's persistent trust records

notes.text: Supervisor judgment on R-281's security decisions: (1) scope to the selected project and run temp, never persist trust: accepted. (2) Codex per-launch inline projects trust: accepted (trust grants no write). Claude: rejected as built. --add-dir of context.worktrees makes every sibling lane a working directory, which Claude's file tools may edit; Monitor's deny rules cover peer projects only, so a worker could edit other lanes without a prompt (breaks lane isolation). Correction: workers keep their own lane as the working directory; the supervisor and any reader get read-only access to the project's worktree root (native Read permission rules plus sandbox allowRead), with no edit or write grants outside their own lane.
notes.summary: Accept the Codex trust part; send the Claude worktree-root add-dir back as read-only access.

notes.text: Supervisor judgment on R-284's security decisions: accepted. Working directories are cwd + run temp only; the project's worktree root is read-only via scoped Read rules and sandbox allowRead; sibling lanes get Edit/shell-write denies and a per-launch PreToolUse write guard; the supervisor reads all lanes and edits none. This is the read-only correction requested on R-281.
notes.summary: Accepted R-284's read-only lane access as the requested correction.

notes.text: R-284 accepted on judgment but not settled yet: my late ingest of R-281 (after R-284) made R-281 the item's outcome, so settle refuses R-284. ENG-253 fixes outcome ordering; settle R-284 after it lands. Lesson: ingest an escalated original before its correction reports.
